question: Should OpenClaw own Twilio RCS as a bundled channel, or should this implementation ship as a ClawHub plugin with only any missing generic plugin API added to core?
rationale: The existing plugin seams cover nearly the entire channel, but the branch also proposes a generic route-registration result and changes SMS startup behavior; deciding whether RCS demand and maintenance burden justify bundling is product ownership, not a mechanical review choice.

options.title: ClawHub plus narrow core seam
options.body: Publish RCS as a ClawHub channel plugin after fixing the provider contracts and proof, with a separate focused core PR only for the generic route-ownership API if external plugins require it.

options.title: Sponsor bundled RCS
options.body: Accept long-term core ownership, then require the provider-contract fixes, live Twilio proof, dependency approval, compatibility documentation, and upgrade validation before merge.

options.title: Decline the channel
options.body: Close the implementation if maintainers do not want either bundled ownership or a supported generic seam for an external RCS plugin.

recommendation.title: ClawHub plus narrow core seam
recommendation.body: Publish RCS as a ClawHub channel plugin after fixing the provider contracts and proof, with a separate focused core PR only for the generic route-ownership API if external plugins require it.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest routing precedent is the bundled SMS channel introduced under this person's feature history, and repository policy identifies this handle for maintainer decisions.
